book.subject: ict
book.title: ICT Grade 8
book.source: Information and Communication Technology Grade 8, Ministry of Education, State of Eritrea

units.title: Basic Concepts of ICT
units.intro: This unit explains **ICT** and **information literacy**, the **kinds of computers**, the **hardware** parts and the **three main software**, and the difference between **data and information**.

pins.text: IT hardware: computers, scanners, digital video and still cameras
CT equipment: phones, faxes, modems and computers
hardware: the physical parts you can see or touch
hard disk drive (HDD): inside the system unit, stores large amounts of data
BIOS: Basic Input Output System; read when the computer is turned on
Operating System: controls the way the computer works and controls the hardware
Application Software: helps the user do specific tasks (e.g. MS Office)
information: the meaning we attach to data
example: a red traffic light is data
the meaning, STOP, is the information

cards.title: ICT in our lives
body: **ICT** (Information and Communications Technology) is part of our **everyday life**.
ICT literacy is almost a **requirement** for work, social and personal life.
ICT in education **improves the quality** of teaching and learning.

cards.title: What is a computer?
body: A **computer** is an **electronic device** that:
- **accepts** data,
- **processes** it,
- **gives it out** processed,
- **stores** it for later use.

cards.title: Memory trick: A-P-G-S
body: "**A**ll **P**upils **G**et **S**mart" = Accept, Process, Give out, Store.

cards.title: Information Technology (IT)
body: **IT** = the **hardware** (equipment) and **software** (programs) that let us access, store, organize and present information electronically.
Hardware: computers, scanners, digital video and still cameras.
Software: browsers, databases, operating systems, application programs.

cards.title: Communications Technology (CT)
body: **CT** = telecommunications equipment used to **send and share** information.
Examples: **phones, faxes, modems** and **computers**.

cards.title: IT and CT equipment
body: Tap the dots.

cards.title: ICT and information literacy
body: **ICT** = using **IT and CT together**: accessing, selecting, processing and sharing knowledge and information.
**Information literacy**: the knowledge, skills and attitudes to take part in society in the information age.
An information literate learner can **select, interpret, evaluate, present and share** information.

cards.q: Which of these is an example of Communications Technology (CT) in the book?
cards.why: p. 2: CT examples are phones, faxes, modems and computers.

cards.title: Many kinds
body: Computers differ by **size, shape** and **processing power**.
Common types: **desktop** (PC), **laptop**, **PDA** and **mainframe**.

cards.title: Types of computers
body: Tap each computer.

cards.title: Desktop computers
body: Also called **personal computers (PC)**.
Used in offices, school labs, homes, training centres and internet cafes.
They have a **separate** monitor, keyboard, mouse and system unit.

cards.title: A typical desktop computer
body: Tap each part (Fig. 1.6).

cards.title: Laptop computers
body: A **laptop** is also called a **notebook**. Its key features:
- **portable**: all parts are in one,
- **light weight**,
- **low power** use,
- does **not** make too much **heat**.

cards.q: What is another name for a laptop?
cards.why: "Laptop computer, also known as notebook" (p. 3).

cards.title: Hardware and software
body: A computer system has **two parts**: **hardware** and **software**.

cards.title: Hardware
body: **Hardware** is all the **devices** that make up a computer.
It is the **physical** part you can **see or touch**.
Some parts are hidden **inside the system unit**.

cards.title: Four main hardware parts
body: Tap the dots.

cards.title: Input devices
body: **Input devices** help to **enter data** into the computer.
They send data to the computer to be processed.

cards.title: Input devices
body: Tap each device.

cards.title: Output devices
body: **Output devices** show the output processed by the computer.
Output can be **soft copy** (on the screen), **hard copy** (printout), **audio** or **video**.

cards.title: Output devices
body: Tap each device.

cards.title: The CPU
body: The **Central Processing Unit (CPU)** processes data.
It is the computer's **brain**: it controls all calculations and processing.

cards.title: Storage devices
body: **Storage devices** store data for **later use**.
The **hard disk drive (HDD)** is inside the system unit. It stores **large amounts** of data. All the vital programs are installed on it.

cards.title: Storage devices
body: Tap each device.

cards.title: Software
body: **Software** is a set of **instructions** that make the hardware work.
Software **cannot be touched**.
Two groups: **system software** and **application software**.

steps.text: **BIOS** (Basic Input Output System) handles the flow of data between the computer and its input/output devices. It is read when the computer is **turned on or restarted**.
The **Operating System (OS)** controls the way a computer works. It **controls the hardware** directly. Examples: DOS, Windows XP, Windows 7, Windows 8, Unix, Linux.
**Application software** helps the user do **specific tasks**. Examples: MS Office, business, medical, accounting and gaming software.

cards.title: Memory trick: B-O-A
body: Think of a **BOA**t: the three software a computer must have.

cards.q: Which part is called the computer's brain?
cards.why: The CPU "is considered as the computer's brain" (p. 7).

cards.title: Raw data
body: **Data** = **raw facts and figures** before they are processed.
Data has **no meaning** until it is processed: calculated, sorted or organized.

steps.text: Start with **data**: raw facts and figures.
**Process** it: calculate, sort or organize. This is called **data processing**.
The result is **information**: the meaning we attach to the data.
Example: a **red traffic light** is data...
...and its meaning, **STOP**, is the information.

cards.title: Data or information? (Exercise 1.2)
head: Example
Data or information?
rows: A man gave his three kids 35, 50 and 100 Nakfa for their weekend vacation
information (the figures now have a meaning)

cards.title: Key terms of Unit 1
body: application software, BIOS, computer, CPU, drive, hard disk, hardware, input devices, operating system, output devices, storage devices.

cards.q: "35 Nakfa, 50 Nakfa, 100 Nakfa" alone is...
cards.why: They are raw figures with no meaning attached, so they are data (p. 9).

glossary.meaning: Information and Communications Technology
Information Technology: hardware and software for information
Communications Technology: equipment to send and share information
an electronic device that accepts, processes, gives out and stores data
the skills to select, interpret, evaluate, present and share information
personal computer; a desktop computer
a portable computer, also called a notebook
personal digital assistant
the physical parts of a computer you can touch
a device that enters data into the computer
a device that shows the processed output
Central Processing Unit, the computer's brain
a device that stores data for later use
hard disk drive: stores large amounts of data inside the system unit
instructions that make the hardware work; cannot be touched
Basic Input Output System
software that controls the computer and its hardware
programs that help the user do specific tasks
raw facts and figures
the meaning we attach to data

tips.text: Input = **into** the computer (keyboard, mouse). Output = **out of** the computer (monitor, printer).
Hardware can be **touched**; software **cannot**.
Learn the full names: **CPU**, **BIOS**, **HDD**, **PDA**, **PC**, **ICT**.
Data + meaning = **information**.

items.text: A laptop is also known as a ___.
Desktop computers use more power than laptops.
The mouse is an output device.
CDs and DVDs are storage devices.
The operating system controls the hardware.
Medical software is an operating system.

cards.back: accepts, processes, gives out and stores data
select, interpret, evaluate, present and share information

questions.q: An electronic machine that accepts, processes and gives out processed data is a...
why: p. 1: a computer accepts data, processes it, gives it out and stores it.
questions.tip: Look for the definition on p. 1.

similar.q: What else does a computer do with data?
similar.a: it stores it for later use

questions.q: A student can select, interpret, present and share information well. The student is...
why: p. 2: when learners become information literate they can select, interpret, evaluate, present and share information.
questions.tip: These verbs are the definition of information literacy.

similar.q: Define information literacy.
similar.a: the knowledge, understanding, skills and attitudes learners need to take part in society in the information age

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a type of computer?
why: p. 2–3: PC, laptop (notebook) and PDA are all types of computers.

similar.q: Name four types of computers.
similar.a: desktop (PC), laptop, PDA, mainframe

questions.q: Identify the area where computers are NOT used.
why: p. 3: desktops are used in offices, school labs, homes, training centres and internet cafes.
ICT is part of our everyday life (p. 1).
questions.tip: "none" means computers are used in all of them.

similar.q: Where are desktop computers used?
similar.a: offices, school labs, homes, computer training centers, internet cafes

questions.q: A desktop is different from a laptop because it has a separate system unit, monitor, mouse and keyboard.
why: p. 3: desktops have separate parts; a laptop has all its parts integrated in one.

similar.q: Name two other key features of a laptop.
similar.a: light weight and low power consumption (also: little heat)

questions.q: The hard disk drive is also called the brain of the computer.
why: p. 7: the CPU is the brain.
The HDD stores data and programs.

similar.q: What is the function of the HDD?
similar.a: to store large amounts of data; programs are installed and saved on it

questions.q: BIOS is a set of instructions that tells the computer how to handle the flow of data.
why: p. 8 definition of BIOS.

similar.q: When does the computer read the BIOS?
similar.a: when it is turned on or restarted

questions.q: CPU stands for Central ___ Unit.
why: p. 7: Central Processing Unit.

similar.q: What does BIOS stand for?
similar.a: Basic Input Output System

questions.q: Write three input devices and three output devices.
questions.answer: Input: keyboard, mouse, scanner (also webcam, microphone, joystick, digital camera). Output: monitor, printer, speaker (also LCD projector).
why: p. 5: input devices, Figs. 1.10–1.16.
p. 6: output devices.
questions.tip: In = you give to the computer. Out = the computer gives to you.

similar.q: What is the function of output devices?
similar.a: to provide or display output processed by the computer

questions.q: What is the difference between data and information?
questions.answer: Data is raw facts and figures before processing. Information is the meaning we attach to data after it is processed.
why: Example: a red traffic light (data) means STOP (information).

similar.q: Is "10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15" data or information?
similar.a: data

questions.q: Which is an example of an operating system?
why: p. 8: operating systems include DOS, Windows XP, Windows 7, Windows 8, Unix, Linux.

similar.q: Name one example of application software.
similar.a: MS Office (also business, medical, accounting, gaming software)

questions.q: A printout is a...
why: p. 6: soft copy = screen display; hard copy = printout.

similar.q: What is a soft copy?
similar.a: a screen display

units.title: Introduction to Computer Operations
units.intro: This unit teaches **Microsoft Windows 7**: the **desktop**, the **mouse and keyboard**, **files and folders**, the **Start menu**, windows, and how to **restart and shut down** a computer.

pins.text: press the power button on the system unit
Windows 7 starts automatically after the BIOS
a logon screen may ask for your username and password
Computer icon: see the drives and their files
Documents: a storage place for your personal files
Recycle Bin: stores deleted files until you empty it
Internet Explorer: Windows' built-in web browser
Taskbar: shows programs and files that are open
an open window on the desktop (the work area)
scroller: scrolls within a page, like the scroll bars
Step 1: right-click on empty space on the desktop
Step 4: type "Eritrea" and click on empty space
a file, e.g. hanna123.docx: name "hanna123" + extension ".docx"
Shut down: the computer turns off
Restart: the computer turns off and starts up again
title bar: shows the name of the open resource
drag a corner (two sided arrow) to re-size
Account Name (e.g. "ICT Lab"): your personal files in one place
All Programs: programs installed, including Microsoft Office

cards.title: Windows 7
body: An **operating system** manages the computer hardware.
The most common ones are **Microsoft Windows** operating systems.
This book uses **Windows 7**.

steps.text: Press the **power button** on the system unit.
The **BIOS** runs first.
**Windows 7 starts automatically** after the BIOS.
A **logon** screen may ask for your **username** and **password**. Type the password and press **Enter**.
The **desktop** appears.

cards.title: The Windows 7 desktop
body: Tap the dots.

cards.title: The desktop
body: The **desktop** is the **main Windows 7 screen**.
It is the **work area** where dialog boxes, windows, icons and menus appear.
You can change how it looks to suit you.

cards.title: Desktop icons
head: Icon
What it does
rows: shows the drives (hard disk, CD/DVD, flash disk, SD card) and their files
a storage place for your personal files; shows your username
stores deleted files until you empty it

cards.title: The taskbar
body: The **taskbar** shows programs or files that are **open**. Click its buttons to go between them.
In Windows 7 it also holds **shortcuts** to programs you use often.

cards.title: Pin a program to the taskbar
body: 1. **Right-click** an icon in the Start menu.
2. Choose **Pin to Taskbar**.
3. Click that icon to open the program.
You can pin as many icons as fit on the taskbar.

cards.title: Quick view
body: Put the mouse pointer over an **open program** on the taskbar.
You see a small **preview** of all its open windows. Click one to bring it to the front.

cards.q: Which desktop icon keeps deleted files until you empty it?
cards.why: "Recycle Bin icon – Stores any files you deleted until you empty it" (p. 13).

cards.title: The mouse
body: The **mouse** is a frequently used **input device**.
On screen it is shown by the **mouse pointer**.
When you point at an icon, a **pop-up description** gives information about it.

cards.title: Parts of the mouse
body: Tap the three parts.

cards.title: Hands on Activity 2.1
head: To do this...
...use this action
rows: click on free space on the desktop
press, hold the left button and drag

cards.title: The keyboard
body: The **keyboard** is an **input device** for **text, numbers and commands**.
Most keyboards use the **QWERTY** layout. The name comes from the first letters on the **top row**.
It is easy to use and allows **fast entry** of text. You can **check** your typing because it appears on the screen at the same time.

cards.title: Four parts of the keyboard
body: Tap each part.

cards.title: Memory trick: F-N-T-N
body: "**F**our **N**ice **T**yping **N**otes."

cards.title: Some keys on a standard keyboard
head: Key
Where
rows: Tab, Capitals Lock, Shift, Control, Window
left side of the typing pad
right side of the typing pad
top right, above the numeric pad

cards.title: Typing properly
body: Proper **body, hand and finger positions** are very important for **healthy use** and **fast typing**.
Use the **left hand** for the left half of the keyboard and the **right hand** for the right half.

cards.q: Where does the name QWERTY come from?

options.B: the keys on the top row

cards.why: "this name comes from the keys on the top row, which spell out QWERTY" (p. 16).

cards.title: Files
body: All information in a computer is stored in **files**.
A **file** is a collection of digital data: documents, photos, audio, video.
A filename has **two parts**: the **name** and the **extension** (the type of file).
Examples: **hanna123.docx**, **omer said.xlsx**.

cards.title: Folders
body: Windows saves files in **folders**. A folder is like a **master file**.
A folder can contain files or other folders, called **sub folders**.

steps.text: **Right-click** on empty space on the desktop.
Put the mouse pointer on **New**.
Click **Folder**. A "New folder" appears.
Type **Eritrea** and click on empty space.

cards.title: Rename or delete
body: **Right-click** the folder and choose **Rename** or **Delete**.
Or click the folder **once** and press **Delete** on the keyboard.

cards.title: Folders, sub folders and files
body: Tap the dots.

cards.title: Making a sub folder
body: To make a sub folder "Asmara" inside "Eritrea":
1. **Double-click** "Eritrea" to open it.
2. Follow the same steps as for a new folder.
Sub folders can contain sub-sub folders. This is very useful for **archiving** documents.

cards.title: Copy and paste, or cut and paste
body: 1. **Select** the folder.
2. **Right-click** it and click **Copy** or **Cut**.
3. **Go to** the drive where you want the data, and paste.

cards.q: In the filename "hanna123.docx", what is ".docx"?
cards.why: A filename has a name and an extension; the extension refers to the type of file (p. 18).

cards.title: The Start menu
body: The **Start menu** is the **starting point** in Windows 7: all programs and settings can be reached from it.
Open it with the **Windows icon** button at the bottom left, or press the **Windows key**.

cards.title: The Start menu
body: Tap the dots.

cards.title: Parts of an open window
body: Tap the dots.

cards.title: Window buttons
body: The **title bar** at the top shows the **name** of what is open.
On the right: **Minimize** and **Maximize (Restore Down)** change the size. **Close** closes the window.
To **re-size**: point at a corner, get a **two sided arrow**, and drag.

cards.title: Shut down or restart?

states.label: Shut down
states.text: Click **Start**, then **Shut down**. Windows saves your computer settings, then turns off. Your **work is not saved**: save it first! Using Shut down helps your **hard disk drive live longer**.

states.label: Restart
states.text: **Restart** is like Shut down, but the computer **starts up again**. Your work is **not saved**: save it first!

body: Move the slider.

cards.title: Key terms of Unit 2
body: close, desktop, file, folder, keyboard, maximize, minimize, mouse, password,
power buttons, restart, restore, shut down, start menu, sub folder, windows 7, username.

cards.q: What must you do before you shut down or restart?
cards.why: With Shut down and Restart "your work will not be saved", so you must save it manually first (p. 24).

tips.text: Mouse: **click** = select, **double-click** = open, **right-click** = menu, **drag** = move.
Keyboard parts: **function keys**, **navigation keys**, **typing pad**, **numeric pad**.
Filename = **name** + **extension** (hanna123 + .docx).
New folder = **Right-click → New → Folder**.
Always **save your work** before Shut down or Restart.

items.text: The Recycle Bin stores deleted files until you ___ it.
A folder inside a folder is called a sub ___.
To create a folder: right-click, then ___.
The keyboard is an output device.
A double-click is two rapid clicks.
Shut down saves your work automatically.
items.why: Your work is not saved; save it first (p. 24).

items.text: A file can be a document, a photo or an audio file.
The scroller is used to scroll within a page.

questions.q: The small pictures that appear on your desktop after logging on are called...
why: p. 13: "icons (small pictures)".

similar.q: Name the four usual desktop icons.
similar.a: Computer, Documents, Recycle Bin, Internet Explorer

questions.q: The part of a mouse used to scroll within a page is the...
why: p. 16: "The Scroller button is used to scroll within a page or pages of a document".

similar.q: What is the scroller equal to?
similar.a: using the scroll bars

questions.q: Which of the following can be inserted into a computer using a keyboard?
why: p. 16: the keyboard helps us insert text, numbers and commands.

similar.q: Name the four parts of a keyboard.
similar.a: function keys, navigation keys, typing pad, numeric pad

questions.q: Which of the following is FALSE about the keyboard?

options.C: it enables fast entry of text

why: p. 16: the keyboard is an input device, easy to use, and enables fast entry of text.
questions.tip: Find the one that is not in the text.

similar.q: Give two features of a keyboard.
similar.a: it is easy to use; it enables fast entry of text (you can also check data as it appears)

questions.q: A file can be...
why: p. 18: a file is a collection of digital data such as documents, photos, audio and video files.
questions.tip: All three are in the list.

similar.q: What two parts must a filename have?
similar.a: a name and an extension

questions.q: eriterea12.docx is saved on a desktop. The part ".docx" is called the...
why: p. 18: the extension refers to the type of file.

similar.q: Which part is the name?
similar.a: eriterea12

questions.q: The steps to create a folder are...
why: p. 19: Step 1 right-click on the desktop; Step 2 point to "New"; Step 3 click Folder.

similar.q: How do you delete a folder with the keyboard?
similar.a: click it once, then press Delete

questions.q: Restart is the same as Shut down, except that the computer starts up again.
why: p. 24: "Restart is the same as Shut down except that the computer is started up again".

similar.q: Which button helps the hard disk drive live longer?
similar.a: Shut down

questions.q: On the right side of the title bar are the Minimize, Maximize and ___ buttons.

similar.q: How do you re-size a window?
similar.a: point at a corner, get a two sided arrow, and drag

questions.q: List four tasks a computer mouse can perform.
questions.answer: Any four of: pointing, single-clicking, double-clicking, dragging, right-clicking, scrolling.
why: p. 15: the six mouse actions.

similar.q: What is double-clicking?
similar.a: two rapid clicks

questions.q: How do you open the Start menu?
questions.answer: Click the Windows icon (Start) button in the bottom left corner, or press the Windows key on the keyboard.

similar.q: What is the Account Name in Fig. 2.17?
similar.a: ICT Lab

units.title: Introduction to Microsoft Office Word 2007
units.intro: In this unit you learn **Word 2007**: to **open, create, save and close** documents, **select and edit** text, **format characters** and **paragraphs**, and make **tables**.

pins.text: Step 1: click the Start button on the taskbar
Step 4: click Microsoft Office Word 2007; a blank page appears
title bar: shows the document name
groups of command buttons on the ribbon
New: start a new document from a template
Open: open a document saved earlier
Save: save the current document (first time: opens Save As)
Save As: give a name, or save with a new name or place
Close closes the document (Word keeps running); Exit Word closes Word and all documents
3. type the file name and choose the place
red zigzag underline: a spelling error
green zigzag underline: a grammar error
left: lines line up on the left margin
center: the middles of the lines line up
right: lines line up on the right margin
justify: both sides line up (except the last line); extra space goes between words
a cell: where a row and a column meet
gridlines: the lines that mark the cells

cards.title: What is Word 2007?
body: **Microsoft Office Word 2007** is an **application software** for working with **text documents**.
It is the **most widely used** application software in the world.
The book calls it simply **Word 2007**.

steps.text: Click the **Start** button on the taskbar.
Click **All Programs**.
Click **Microsoft Office**.
Click **Microsoft Office Word 2007**. A **blank page** appears.

cards.title: The Word 2007 screen
body: Tap the dots to learn each part (Fig. 3.2).

cards.title: Title bar and ribbon
body: The **title bar** shows the document name. A new document is called "**Document 1**" until you save it with a name.
The **ribbon** is a set of **eight tabbed toolbars**. Only **one** is visible at a time. The **Home** tab is shown first.
Commands on the ribbon are arranged in **groups**.

cards.title: Minimize the ribbon
body: **Double-click** the active tab to minimize the ribbon.
Click any tab to show it again.

cards.title: Office button commands
body: Tap each command.

steps.text: Click the **Office button**.
Choose **Save**.
Type the **file name** and choose **where** to save it.
Click **Save**.

cards.title: Why save?
body: The computer's memory keeps your work only **for a while**.
When the computer restarts or shuts down, **unsaved work is lost**.
So **save** your work on the **hard disk**. To save in another place, use **Save As**.

cards.title: Keyboard shortcuts (3.1)
head: Keys
What they do
rows: Save (opens the Save As dialog box the first time)

cards.title: Closing and opening
body: Click the **Close** button (X) at the top right to close the document.
If you close without saving, Word asks if you want to **save** the changes.
To open a saved document: **Office button → Open**, find the document, click **Open**.

cards.q: Why must you save your work on the hard disk?

options.B: because unsaved work is lost when the computer restarts or shuts down

cards.why: p. 30: after a restart or shut down, the unsaved document cannot be got again.

cards.title: Inserting a symbol
body: For symbols **not on the keyboard**:
1. Put the **cursor** where you want the symbol.
2. Click the **Insert** tab, then **Symbol**.
3. Click a symbol, or **More Symbols**, choose one, click **Insert**, then **Close**.

cards.title: Moving in a document
body: Use the **arrow (navigation) keys** to move up, down, left and right.
Or use the **scroll bars**.

cards.title: Undo and redo
head: Command
What it does
Shortcut
rows: brings back a change, e.g. restores text you deleted by mistake

cards.title: Select first!
body: **Selecting** = **highlighting** text with the mouse or keyboard.
You must **select text first** before you cut, copy, delete, format or move it.

cards.title: Selecting with the mouse
body: 1. Put the pointer at the **beginning or end** of the text.
2. **Hold down the left button** and move to the other end.
3. **Release** the button.

cards.q: Which shortcut undoes a change?
cards.why: "Ctrl + Z for Undo and Ctrl + Y for Redo" (p. 34).

cards.title: What is formatting?
body: **Formatting** = changing the **appearance** of a document.
Basic formats: **Bold**, **Italic**, **Underline**. Select the text first, then click the format on the **Home** tab.

cards.title: How formatted text looks
body: Tap each box.

cards.title: Memory trick: B-I-U
body: The shortcut letter is the **first letter** of the format.

cards.title: The Font dialog box
body: More options are in the **Font dialog box**. Open it with the small **launcher** at the corner of the **Font group**.
It has **two tabs**: **Font** and **Character Spacing**.

cards.title: Font options
head: Option
Examples
rows: red, orange, green, blue, purple, brown...

cards.title: Character spacing
body: Character Spacing can **stretch or contract** text.
It can **increase or decrease** the space between characters.
It can make **raised** or **lowered** characters.

cards.title: Styles
body: A **style** includes typeface, size, effects (bold, italic, underline) and colours.
The **Home** tab has areas that control style: **Font**, **Paragraph** and **Styles**.

cards.title: Font face, size and colour
body: **Typeface**: click the arrow next to the font name.
**Size**: click the arrow on the font size, or the increase/decrease buttons.
**Colour**: click the arrow next to the font colour button.

cards.title: More character tools
head: Tool
What it does
rows: marks text like a marker pen
copies formatting to other text (Clipboard group)

cards.q: What does an italic text look like?
cards.why: "A text is said to be italicized if its appearance is inclined" (p. 35).

cards.title: Paragraph tools
body: Paragraph formatting changes the look of the **whole document**.
Find the tools on the **Page Layout** tab or the **Paragraph group** of the Home tab.

cards.title: Four types of alignment

states.label: Left
states.text: The **left** ends of the lines line up along the left margin.

states.label: Center
states.text: The **middles** of the lines line up at the centre.

states.label: Right
states.text: The **right** ends of the lines line up along the right margin.

states.label: Justify
states.text: Both ends line up and all lines are the **same length** (except the last). Extra space is put **between words**.

body: Move the slider.

cards.title: Line spacing
body: **Line spacing** = the distance between the **lines** of a paragraph.
Names: **single**, **1.5 lines**, **double**. Numbers: **2.0 = double**.
Use the **Line Spacing** button in the Paragraph group.

cards.title: Paragraph spacing and indents
body: **Paragraph spacing**: space **before and after** paragraphs (Add Space Before / After).
**Indent**: extra empty space between the **margin** and the text.
Use the **Increase Indent** and **Decrease Indent** buttons.

cards.title: Spelling and grammar
body: Word marks errors while you type:
- **red zigzag** underline = **spelling** error,
- **green zigzag** underline = **grammar** error.
Names may not be in Word's dictionary, so they may get red lines.

cards.title: Checking spelling and grammar
body: 1. Open the document.
2. Click the **Review** tab.
3. Choose **Spelling and Grammar**.
4. Choose an option: **ignore once**, **ignore** it, or **change** it to the suggestion.

cards.q: A green zigzag underline shows...
cards.why: "spelling errors are indicated by red zigzag underline, grammar errors are indicated by green zigzag underline" (p. 43–44).

cards.title: Parts of a table
body: Tap the dots.

cards.title: What is a table?
body: A **table** is a grid of **rows** and **columns** that meet to form **cells**.
The lines around the cells are **gridlines**.
Tables can show text, graphics and pictures.

cards.title: Creating a table
body: 1. Put the **cursor** where you want the table.
2. **Insert** tab → **Table** → **Insert Table**.
3. Type the number of **columns** and **rows**.
4. Click **OK**.

cards.title: Inserting rows and columns
body: **Right-click** a cell → **Insert** →
**Insert Rows Above** or **Insert Rows Below**,
or **Insert Columns to the Left** or **to the Right**.

cards.title: Merge, split, delete
body: **Merge**: join two or more cells next to each other into **one cell** (select, right-click, **Merge Cells**).
**Split**: divide a cell into more rows or columns (right-click, **Split Cells**, give the numbers, OK).
**Delete**: right-click, **Delete Cells**; Word asks to shift cells **left or up**.

cards.q: Joining two or more cells next to each other into one cell is called...
cards.why: "Combining two or more consecutive cells... into a single cell is called Merging" (p. 47).

glossary.meaning: Microsoft Office Word 2007, a program for text documents
the set of tabbed toolbars at the top of Word
a labelled part of the ribbon, like Home or Insert
a set of related buttons on a ribbon tab
the round button with file commands (New, Open, Save...)
a ready design for a new document
save with a new name or in a new place
the blinking line where you type
a sign not on the keyboard
take back the last change
do again what Undo took back
highlight text to work on it
changing how a document looks
dark, thick text
slanted text
a line under text
the style and shape of letters
a set of formats: typeface, size, effects, colours
colour behind text, like a marker
how the lines of a paragraph line up
line up both sides of a paragraph
the distance between lines
empty space between the margin and the text
a grid of rows and columns
a box where a row and a column meet
join cells into one
divide one cell into more

tips.text: Always **select** text before you format it.
Shortcuts: **Ctrl+B** bold, **Ctrl+I** italic, **Ctrl+U** underline, **Ctrl+Z** undo, **Ctrl+Y** redo, **Ctrl+S** save.
Red zigzag = **spelling**; green zigzag = **grammar**.
Four alignments: **left, center, right, justify**.
Save **often**; unsaved work is lost at shut down.

items.text: A new document is called "Document ___" until you save it.
Line spacing 2.0 is the same as ___ spacing.
Spelling errors have a ___ zigzag underline.
You must select text before formatting it.
Justify puts extra space between words.
Close closes Word and all documents.
items.why: That is Exit Word. Close closes only the current document.

items.text: A table is a grid of rows and columns.

questions.q: What is the most common way to start Word 2007?

options.B: using the Start button on the taskbar

why: p. 26: "the most commonly used way is to use the Start button on the Windows taskbar".
questions.tip: Start → All Programs → Microsoft Office → Word.

similar.q: What appears after you click Word 2007?
similar.a: a blank Word page

questions.q: Which Office button command closes Word together with all open documents?
why: p. 29: "Exit Word: closes the Word 2007 program together with all open documents."
Close keeps Word running.

similar.q: What does Close do?
similar.a: closes the current document; Word keeps running

questions.q: Clicking Save on a document that was never saved opens the Save As dialog box.
why: p. 29: Save saves if the document has a name; otherwise it launches the Save As dialog box.

similar.q: Which command saves a copy in another place?
similar.a: Save As

questions.q: Which shortcut is Redo?
why: p. 34: Ctrl + Y for Redo.

similar.q: What does Redo do?
similar.a: the opposite of Undo

questions.q: Ctrl + ___ makes selected text underlined.
why: p. 35: Ctrl + U underlines.

similar.q: Which shortcut makes text bold?
similar.a: Ctrl + B

questions.q: The two tabs of the Font dialog box are...
why: p. 35: "The Font dialog box has two tabs. 1. Font 2. Character Spacing".
questions.tip: One is about letters, one about spaces.

similar.q: Name three font options.
similar.a: font family, font style, font size (also colour, underline style)

questions.q: In which alignment are all lines (except the last) the same length?
why: p. 42: with justified alignment the lines are all of the same length; extra space goes between words.

similar.q: Where are the tools for alignment?
similar.a: the Paragraph group on the Home tab

questions.q: To check spelling and grammar, which tab do you click?
why: p. 44: click the Review tab, then Spelling and Grammar.

similar.q: What colour shows a spelling error?
similar.a: red zigzag underline

questions.q: The lines that mark the cell boundaries in a table are called gridlines.

similar.q: Where do rows and columns meet?
similar.a: in cells

questions.q: The teacher forgot Nebiat (80) after Halima. How can she add the row using "Insert Rows Below"?
questions.answer: Right-click a cell in Halima's row, move to Insert, choose Insert Rows Below, then type Nebiat's information.
why: p. 46 worked example.

similar.q: How would she do it with "Insert Rows Above"?
similar.a: right-click a cell in Jaefer's row, Insert, Insert Rows Above, then type Nebiat's information

questions.q: In the review, Ali scored English 95, Mathematics 84, Social Studies 93, Natural science 96. Give each grade: A if 95 or more, B if less than 95 but more than 90, C if less than 90.
questions.answer: English A, Mathematics C, Social Studies B, Natural science A.
why: 93 is less than 95 but more than 90 → B.
84 is less than 90 → C.

similar.q: Which subject was his mother not happy with?
similar.a: mathematics

questions.q: To add a column "Section" between "Name" and "Score", you right-click a Name cell and choose...
why: p. 47: right-click, Insert, then Insert Columns to the Left or to the Right.
The new column must be on the right of "Name".
questions.tip: New column goes to the right of the cell you click.

similar.q: What else could you right-click to do the same?
similar.a: a Score cell, then Insert Columns to the Left

units.title: Social and Ethical Issues of IT
units.intro: This unit is about using computers **safely and wisely**: **health problems (RSI)** and how to avoid them, harm to the **environment**, **computer misuse**, and **computer viruses**.

pins.text: monitor screen tilted upwards at an angle
an adjustable chair helps good posture
Repetitive Strain Injuries (RSI) and other risks
computers contain toxic metals, acids, plastics and biologically active materials
so: recycle, or dispose of them safely
a virus copies itself and harms the computer
infected external storage devices, like a flash disk
downloading infected files from the Internet
protecting a computer from a virus attack
use up-to-date anti-virus software (e.g. Avast, Avira)
no illegal software; no CD or DVD from an unknown source
download only from a reputable site
2000: an email headed "I Love You" infected many computers around the world
now: about ten to fifteen new viruses appear every day

cards.title: Computers everywhere
body: People use computers in schools, banks, shops, offices, factories, hospitals and universities.
Computers made our lives **easier, faster** and **more organized**.

cards.title: RSI
body: Computers may cause **physical injury, headache** and **vision problems** if not used wisely.
These are called **Repetitive Strain Injuries (RSI)**.
They are caused by doing the **same actions over and over again**.

cards.title: A healthy sitting position
body: Tap the dots (Fig. 4.1).

cards.title: Six pieces of advice
head: No.
Advice
rows: avoid poor posture: sit straight, feet flat, eyes 50–70 cm from the screen, wrists not bent
place the monitor screen upwards at an angle
use a protection shield on the monitor
use decreased light on your desktop or monitor

cards.title: Memory trick: 40 and 50–70
body: "**Forty** minutes, then rest; **fifty to seventy** centimetres is best."

cards.title: Health risks of computers
body: Tap the dots.

cards.title: Health risks and solutions (Table 4.1)
head: Health risk
Possible solutions
rows: adjustable chair; foot rests; tilted screen
correct angle for keyboard and mouse; wrist rest; ergonomic keyboard
regular breaks; keep distance from the screen; anti-glare screen; eye tests
anti-glare screen and window blinds; breaks and exercise; eye tests, glasses if needed
good ventilation; change to inkjet printers if possible

steps.text: A computer has hundreds of materials: many are **toxic metals, acids, plastics**.
**Unsafe dumping** of these materials...
...causes **land, water and air pollution**...
...which causes problems for **humans and animals**.
So all toxic materials must be **recycled** or **disposed of safely**.

cards.q: How often should you take a break when using a computer?
cards.why: "taking a break every 40 minutes" (p. 50).

cards.title: Computer misuse
body: **Computer misuse** is using a computer for:
- **hacking**,
- **unauthorized access** to computer systems,
- **purposely spreading** harmful software, such as a **virus**.

cards.title: Unauthorized acts
body: Unauthorized acts include **changing data and software**, **changing passwords and settings** to keep others out, and **interfering** with the system.
Even **trying** to get into a system can lead to **prosecution** (a court case).

cards.title: Copyright
body: Software is protected by **copyright laws**, like music CDs, film DVDs and articles from magazines and books.

cards.title: Rules to obey
body: - Do **not** do unauthorized work.
- Do **not copy** computer programs **illegally**.
- Do **not hack** into a system to see or change information.
- Do **not plant a virus** on someone's computer.

cards.q: Which of these is computer misuse?
cards.why: Computer misuse includes hacking, unauthorized access and spreading viruses (p. 52).

cards.title: What is a virus?
body: A **virus** is a computer program that **copies itself** and is made to **harm** a computer system.
It often attaches itself to **files**.

cards.title: Damage a virus can do
head: Effect
rows: stops the computer from working normally
causes the computer to malfunction (system files)

cards.title: How a virus gets in
body: Tap the four ways.

cards.title: How to protect a computer
body: Tap the four ways.

cards.title: Anti-virus software
body: **Anti-virus software** finds viruses and **removes** or **quarantines** (isolates) infected files.
Examples in the book: **Avast, Avira, McAfee, ESET**.
**Spam** = email messages that advertise something that seems interesting.

steps.text: **1986**: only **one** known computer virus.
**2000**: an email headed "**I Love You**" infected many computers around the world.
Now: about **10 to 15** new viruses appear **every day**.

cards.q: Which is a way a computer gets a virus?
cards.why: p. 53: infected email attachments are one of the four ways listed.

glossary.meaning: Repetitive Strain Injuries: injuries from doing the same actions again and again
the way you sit or stand
tired, sore eyes
a keyboard made to reduce finger and wrist strain
a screen cover that reduces reflection
a gas from laser printers that can irritate
poisonous
use old materials again
throw away
using something in a wrong or illegal way
harmful misuse
getting into a computer system without permission
without permission
a law that protects software, music, films and books from copying
a program that copies itself and harms a computer
software that finds and removes viruses
isolate (keep apart)
emails that advertise something that seems interesting

tips.text: RSI = **R**epetitive **S**train **I**njuries: same action again and again.
Numbers to remember: break every **40 minutes**; eyes **50–70 cm** from the screen.
Virus in: **flash disk, illegal software, downloads, email attachments**. Virus out: **anti-virus, no illegal software, reputable sites, no spam**.
Old computers: **recycle** or **dispose safely**.

games.title: Lets a virus in, or keeps it out?

items.text: Keep your eyes ___ cm away from the screen.
In 1986 there was only ___ known computer virus.
Anti-virus software removes or ___ infected files.
RSI is caused by using the same actions over and over again.
Ozone irritation is caused by laser printers.
Software is not protected by copyright.
items.why: It is protected by copyright laws (p. 52).

items.text: Spam is always safe to open.

cards.back: getting into a system without permission
a program that copies itself and harms a computer

questions.q: Computers made our lives...
why: p. 50: "They made our lives easier, faster and more organized."

similar.q: Name three places where computers are used.
similar.a: schools, banks, hospitals (also shops, offices, factories, universities)

questions.q: Injuries caused by using the same actions over and over again are called...
why: p. 50: Repetitive Strain Injuries or RSI.

similar.q: Give two RSI problems.
similar.a: headache and vision problems (also physical injury)

questions.q: Which is NOT a healthy habit when using a computer?

options.C: using a protection shield on the screen

why: p. 50: take a break every 40 minutes, not 120.

similar.q: How far should your eyes be from the screen?

questions.q: Which of the following is harmful for our environment?
why: p. 52: unsafe dumping causes land, water and air pollution.

similar.q: What must be done with a computer's toxic materials?
similar.a: recycle them or dispose of them safely

questions.q: Which of the following is computer misuse?

options.C: planting a virus on another computer

why: p. 52: computer misuse includes hacking, unauthorized access and spreading viruses.
questions.tip: All three are in the definition.

similar.q: Can just trying to get into a system lead to prosecution?
similar.a: yes

questions.q: A computer program designed to harm a computer by copying itself is...
why: p. 53 definition of a virus.

similar.q: Name two damages a virus causes.
similar.a: stops the computer working normally; corrupts stored data

questions.q: Which is a method to protect a computer from a virus attack?
why: p. 53: all three are listed ways to protect a computer.
questions.tip: All three are in the list.

similar.q: Name two anti-virus programs from the book.
similar.a: Avast and Avira (also McAfee, ESET)

questions.q: In 2000, an email headed "I Love You" infected many computers around the world.

similar.q: How many new viruses appear every day now?
similar.a: about ten to fifteen

questions.q: An ___ keyboard helps reduce finger and wrist damage.
why: p. 51, Table 4.1.

similar.q: What helps reduce eyestrain?
similar.a: anti-glare screens, regular breaks, keeping distance from the screen

questions.q: List two ways of handling a used computer without harming the environment.
questions.answer: Recycle its materials, or dispose of it safely.
why: p. 52: all the toxic materials have to be recycled or disposed of safely.
questions.tip: R and D: Recycle, Dispose safely.

similar.q: What pollution can unsafe dumping cause?
similar.a: land, water and air pollution

questions.q: Write three ways a computer can be infected by a virus.
questions.answer: Any three: infected external storage devices (flash disk), copying illegal software, downloading infected files from the Internet, opening infected email attachments.
why: p. 53 list.

similar.q: What does anti-virus software do?
similar.a: detects viruses and removes or quarantines infected files

units.title: Microsoft Office Excel 2007
units.intro: This unit teaches **Excel 2007**: the **screen**, **workbooks and worksheets**, entering and editing **data**, **rows and columns**, **formatting cells**, **sorting**, **AutoFill**, **formulas and functions**, and **charts**.

pins.text: ribbon: tabs with groups and tools
Name Box: shows the address of the active cell
Formula bar: shows what is in the active cell
worksheets: single sheets inside the workbook
a new workbook opens with three blank worksheets
arrow keys: one cell up, down, left or right
Tab: one cell right; Shift + Tab: one cell left
Page Up / Page Down: one page up or down
ascending: A to Z, smallest to largest
descending: Z to A, largest to smallest
2. point at the black square at the bottom right: the fill handle
3. click and drag across the range; Excel copies the content
clustered column: compares values across categories
stacked column: shows each item as part of the whole

cards.title: What is Excel?
body: **Microsoft Excel**, also called a **spreadsheet**, is a Windows application.
It is used for **entering, editing, analyzing and storing** data.
It can **add, subtract, multiply and divide**, **sort** data, and solve simple financial, mathematical and statistical functions.

steps.text: Click the **Start** button.
Select **All Programs**.
Select **Microsoft Office**.
Click **Microsoft Office Excel 2007**.

cards.title: Same as Word
body: You start Excel the **same way** as Word: Start → All Programs → Microsoft Office → the program.

cards.q: Which of these can Excel do?

options.B: enter, edit, analyze and store data

cards.why: p. 56: Excel is used for entering, editing, analyzing and storing data.

cards.title: The Excel 2007 screen
body: Tap the dots.

cards.title: Basic parts
body: - active cell, column headings, row headings,
- formula bar, Name Box, mouse pointer,
- sheet tabs, worksheet tab scrolling buttons,
- the **ribbon** with tabs, groups and tools.

cards.q: Which of these is NOT a part of the Excel screen?
cards.why: p. 58 lists: active cell, column headings, formula bar, Name Box, mouse pointer, row headings, sheet tabs, tab scrolling buttons and the ribbon. The Recycle Bin is a desktop icon (Unit 2).

cards.title: Workbook and worksheets
body: Tap the dots.

cards.title: Workbook and worksheet
body: A **workbook** is a collection of worksheets in **one file**.
A **worksheet** is a **single sheet** in the workbook. It can hold data, charts or both.
A new workbook opens with **three** blank worksheets.

cards.title: Rows, columns, cells
body: **Rows** go across and are labelled **1, 2, 3**...
**Columns** go down and are labelled **A, B, C**...
A **cell** is where a row and a column meet. Its **address** is column + row, e.g. **B3**.
The first ("Home") cell is **A1**.

cards.title: Moving around with the keyboard
body: Tap each key group.

cards.title: Save, open, exit
body: **Save**: Office button → Save → give a name (e.g. change "Book 1" to "Prize winners list") → Save.
**Open**: Office button → Open → choose the file → Open.
**Exit**: Office button → Exit Excel, or the X, or **Ctrl + W** / **Alt + F4**.

cards.title: Selecting worksheets
head: To select...
do this
rows: click the first tab, hold Shift, click the last
click one tab, hold Ctrl, click others
right-click a tab → Select All Sheets

cards.title: Worksheet tasks (right-click a tab)
head: Task
Steps
rows: right-click a tab → Insert → Worksheet → OK (it goes before that tab)
select tab(s) → right-click → Delete (confirm if it has data)
right-click → Move or Copy → choose workbook and order → OK
right-click → Rename → type → Enter (or double-click the tab)

cards.title: Worksheet name rules
body: - no more than **31 characters**,
- cannot use \ / ? : * [ ],
- cannot be **blank**.

cards.q: The active cell is in column B and row 3. What is its address?
cards.why: The address is the column letter then the row number (p. 60: "the active cell is B3").

cards.title: Three kinds of data
head: Kind
What it is
Alignment
rows: numbers that can be used in calculations; dates are values
mathematical expressions that calculate a value

cards.title: Entering data
body: 1. Click the cell.
2. Type your data.
3. Press **Enter**. The cell **below** becomes active.
The data shows in the cell **and** in the **Formula bar**.

cards.title: Editing data
body: - Double-click the cell, use **Backspace**, and retype.
- Or select the cell and simply **retype**.
- To **clear** a cell, select it and press **Delete**.

cards.q: How are numbers aligned in a cell?
cards.why: p. 67: "Labels are left aligned... Numbers are right aligned in a cell."

cards.title: Default sizes
body: At the start, all columns are **eight characters wide**.
Row heights fit the content, up to **12 points**.

cards.title: Row height and column width
head: To change
Steps
rows: Home tab → Format (Cells group) → Row Height → type → OK (or right-click the row heading)
Home tab → Format → Column Width → type → OK
double-click the border of the column heading

cards.title: Insert rows and columns
body: A new **row** goes **above** the row you select. To insert between rows 7 and 8, select **row 8** → right-click → Insert.
A new **column** goes to the **left** of the column you select. Between C and D, select **column D**.
For **3 rows** between 7 and 8, select rows **8, 9 and 10**.

cards.title: Deleting
body: Select the rows or columns → right-click → **Delete**.
Other rows move **up**; other columns move **left**.

cards.q: To insert 2 columns between columns C and D, which columns do you select?
cards.why: p. 71: "if you want to insert 2 columns between columns C and D, select columns D and E".

cards.title: Formatting a cell
body: Formatting changes **how a cell looks**, not **what is in it**.
Common options: **alignment**, **font**, **border** and **fill**.
Most are in the **Format Cells** dialog box (Home → Format → Format Cells).

cards.title: Alignment and orientation
body: Alignment: **Left, Center, Right, Justify**. By default numbers go **right** and text goes **left**.
**Text orientation** rotates text in a cell: Alignment tab → Orientation → choose the degrees.

cards.title: Font
body: On the **Font** tab choose the **font type** (e.g. Broadway), **size** (e.g. 18), **style** (Regular, Bold, Italic, Bold Italic) and **underline**.
Check the **Preview** box, then OK.

cards.title: Border or fill?
head: Tool
What it does
rows: lines around cells; any colour or thickness; always shows and prints
faint lines between cells on the screen
background colour, pattern colour and pattern style

cards.q: Does formatting a cell change the data in it?
cards.why: "Formatting a cell does not change what's in the cell. Instead it only changes how it looks" (p. 72).

cards.title: Data analysis
body: **Data analysis** = working out the **meaning** of data in a table or chart.

cards.title: Ascending and descending
body: Move the slider. Blank cells always go **last**.

cards.title: Quick sort
body: 1. Select the entries in the column.
2. **Data** tab → **Sort A to Z** or **Sort Z to A** (Sort & Filter group).

cards.q: Sorting numbers in ascending order puts them...
cards.why: p. 77: "Ascending will sort... numerically smallest to largest."

cards.title: What is AutoFill?
body: **AutoFill** uses the **fill handle** to copy data and sequences across a range of cells.

steps.text: Select the cell with the content to copy.
Point at the **black square** at the bottom right corner. The pointer becomes the **fill handle**.
**Click and drag** across the range. Excel copies the content.

cards.q: Where is the fill handle?

options.B: bottom right corner of the cell

cards.why: p. 78: "the black square that appears in the bottom right corner of the cell".

cards.title: Operators and operands
body: In 2 + 3 = 5, **2** and **3** are **operands**; **+** is the **operator**.
A **formula** is an instruction to calculate. It can have operators, operands and functions.

cards.title: Start with =
body: Excel formulas **start** with the equal sign (**=**); in maths class it comes at the end.
Type the formula in the cell where you want the **answer**.

cards.title: Use cell references
body: It is best to use **cell references** (like A1) instead of numbers.
Then Excel **updates** the answer when you change the values.

cards.title: Functions
body: A **function** is a **predefined formula**. Excel 2007 has over **300** functions.
A function has a **name** and **arguments** in brackets, separated by commas.
**Do not** put a space between the name and the bracket: Excel shows an error.

cards.title: Basic functions (Table 5.2)
head: Function
Example
What it does
rows: highest number in C1 to C100
lowest number in D1 to D100

cards.title: Shorter with SUM
body: **=SUM(A1:A7)** is much shorter than **=A1+A2+A3+A4+A5+A6+A7**.
Enter a function by **typing** it, the **fx** button, or **Formulas** tab → Insert Function.

cards.title: AutoSum
body: **AutoSum** adds a group of neighbouring cells automatically.
Select the cells, then click **AutoSum** (the Greek letter **sigma**, Σ) on the Home tab (Editing group) or the Formulas tab.

cards.q: Which symbol is multiplication in Excel?
cards.why: p. 79: multiplication (*), division (/), addition (+), subtraction (-).

cards.title: What is a chart?
body: A **chart** is a **graphical representation** of data in a worksheet.
It can sit **beside the data** (embedded) or on its **own chart sheet**.

cards.title: Types of charts
body: Column, line, pie, bar charts and more. The book focuses on **column charts**.

cards.title: Two column chart sub-types
body: Tap each chart.

cards.title: Creating a column chart
head: Step
What to do
rows: enter the data and highlight all the cells, including headers

cards.title: Key terms of Unit 5
body: alignment, AutoSum, average, border, cell, chart, column, column chart, font, formula, function, Max, min,
operand, operator, sort, sum, text orientation, values, workbook, worksheet.

cards.q: Which column chart compares values across categories?
cards.why: p. 83: "Clustered column charts compare values across categories."

tips.text: Cell address = **column letter first**, then row number: **B3**.
Excel formulas **start with =**. Multiply with *****, divide with **/**.
Labels go **left**, numbers go **right**.
Insert row → select the row **below**; insert column → select the column to the **right**.
SUM adds, AVERAGE averages, MAX highest, MIN lowest, SQRT square root.

items.text: A ___ is a collection of worksheets in one file.
Excel formulas start with the ___ sign.
A new workbook has ___ blank worksheets.
A quick way to copy data from one cell to others is ___.
By default a new workbook has four worksheets.
The junction of a row and a column is a cell.
A formula and a function are the same thing.
items.why: A function is a predefined formula (p. 80).

items.text: A worksheet is a single sheet in the workbook.
A descending sort goes from highest to lowest.

questions.q: Which is NOT true about the AutoFill handle?

options.A: it is at the bottom right corner of the cell
options.C: it is used only with formulas
options.D: it copies content to other cells

why: p. 78: AutoFill copies data and sequences across a range of cells, not only formulas.

similar.q: What does the fill handle look like?
similar.a: a black square at the bottom right corner of the cell

questions.q: Book1 is an example of how ___ are named when you start work.
why: p. 62: you rename "Book 1" when you save the workbook.
Sheets are named Sheet1, Sheet2...

similar.q: What are worksheets called at first?
similar.a: Sheet1, Sheet2, Sheet3

questions.q: Which of the following displays the contents of the active cell?
why: p. 67: the data is displayed in the active cell as well as in the Formula bar.

similar.q: What does the Name Box show?
similar.a: the address of the active cell

questions.q: To open an existing workbook, you click Open from the ___ button.
why: p. 62: "Click on Office Button, choose Open."
questions.tip: File commands are on the Office button.

similar.q: How do you exit Excel?
similar.a: Office button → Exit Excel (or X, Ctrl + W, Alt + F4)

questions.q: In Excel, cell A1 has the formula =3*5+9/3-2. The answer shown is ___.

similar.q: What does =2*4+6/2 give?

questions.q: What is the default alignment of numbers and texts in a cell?
questions.answer: Numbers are aligned to the right; text is aligned to the left.
why: p. 72: "By default, numbers are aligned to the right and texts are aligned to the left."

similar.q: How can you change alignment?
similar.a: Home → Format → Format Cells → Alignment tab

questions.q: How many kinds of data are there in Excel? List them.
why: p. 67: data can be categorized as labels, values and formulas.

similar.q: Which kind is used in calculations?
similar.a: values

questions.q: =SUM(A1:A7) gives the same result as =A1+A2+A3+A4+A5+A6+A7.
why: p. 80: the SUM formula is "considerably shorter than" the long one.

similar.q: What does =MAX(C1:C100) do?
similar.a: returns the highest number from C1 to C100

questions.q: You want to insert one row between rows 7 and 8. Which row do you select?
why: p. 71: "if you want to insert a row between rows 7 and 8, select row 8".

similar.q: Which rows do you select to insert 3 rows between 7 and 8?
similar.a: rows 8, 9 and 10

questions.q: Which worksheet name is NOT allowed?
why: p. 66: the characters \ / ? : * [ ] cannot be used.
"Sales?" has a question mark.

similar.q: What is the longest a worksheet name can be?
similar.a: 31 characters

questions.q: A ___ is a graphical representation of data in a worksheet.

similar.q: What do stacked column charts show?
similar.a: how each item relates to the whole (its contribution to a total)
